common_name: Gasaway Hazelnut (Source of OSU's Eastern Filbert Blight Resistance Breeding Line)

planting.note: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, fertile soil in full sun; Gasaway is maintained mainly in breeding blocks and germplasm collections rather than commercial orchards, since its own nut quality is poor — its value lies in the Eastern Filbert Blight resistance gene it carries.

directions: Gasaway is not cultivated for its own nut crop — it was a chance seedling found growing wild on an Oregon hazelnut farm, bearing nuts of little commercial value, but carrying a single dominant gene that confers strong resistance to Eastern Filbert Blight, the canker disease that devastated susceptible 'Barcelona' plantings across the Pacific Northwest. That gene, now known simply as Gasaway-derived resistance, became the genetic foundation for Oregon State University's entire first generation of EFB-resistant hazelnut releases, including Jefferson, Yamhill, Santiam, and Lagerstedt. Because so many modern commercial cultivars share this single resistance source, breeders have also begun incorporating resistance genes from unrelated backgrounds, such as the Spanish landrace Ratoli, as a hedge against the disease someday evolving past Gasaway's gene alone. Where it is maintained at all, it is grown in breeding blocks and germplasm collections under standard hazelnut culture — full sun and well-drained, slightly acidic soil.
sources: Oregon State University Extension — Hazelnut Cultivar Guide
Oregon State University Hazelnut Breeding Program

common_name: Waco Pecan (Historic Texas Breeding Parent of Zuni)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in late winter while dormant in deep, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Waco is grown today mainly as breeding stock rather than as an orchard variety, and needs a compatible cross-pollinating cultivar nearby since pecans are wind-pollinated.

directions: Waco is an older named Texas pecan grown today almost exclusively as breeding stock rather than as an orchard variety in its own right. Its principal legacy is as a parent, crossed with the widely planted Pawnee, in the USDA Agricultural Research Service breeding work that produced the patented, scab-resistant modern release Zuni. Like other pecans, it should be sited in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with a compatible cross-pollinating cultivar nearby, since pecans are wind-pollinated and most cultivars bear poorly without a partner tree. A spring foliar zinc spray is a standard precaution for pecans generally, since zinc deficiency is common across the alkaline soils of the Texas pecan belt where Waco originated.
sources: USDA Agricultural Research Service — Pecan Breeding Program
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Pecan Variety Selection
